title: Smart Agriculture System using Data Science (IC-ready React + Motoko)

requirements.text: Implement a clean dashboard UI with separate pages for: (1) Crop Yield Prediction, (2) Plant Disease Detection (leaf image upload), (3) Smart Irrigation Recommendation, plus a (4) Data Visualization page that summarizes results across modules.

quotes:
Features:
- Clean dashboard UI
- Separate pages for each module

Extra:
- Add data visualization dashboard

acceptanceCriteria: App has a persistent navigation (sidebar or top nav) linking to Dashboard, Crop Yield, Disease Detection, Irrigation, Visualizations.
Each module page contains an input form, a submit action, a results panel, and clear empty/loading/error states.
All user-facing text is in English.

requirements.text: Add a coherent, distinctive visual theme and apply it consistently (colors, typography, spacing, card styles, form controls) across all pages without using a blue/purple primary palette.
acceptanceCriteria: Theme is applied consistently across layout, buttons, inputs, charts, and cards.
Primary colors are not blue/purple.

requirements.text: Create a Motoko backend (single main actor) that exposes typed APIs for the three modules and stores per-user history of predictions/results in stable storage.

quotes:
Features:
- API endpoints for ML models
- Error handling
- Database schema

acceptanceCriteria: Backend provides update calls for: crop yield prediction, disease detection request submission (metadata), and irrigation recommendation.
Backend provides query calls to list the authenticated user’s past results for each module.
Data persists across canister upgrades using stable variables (no external DB).
All endpoints return structured error variants for invalid inputs.

requirements.text: Crop Yield Prediction module: implement an end-to-end flow that accepts inputs (Soil Type, Rainfall mm, Temperature °C, Humidity %, Fertilizer Usage), returns Predicted Yield (tons/hectare) and an Accuracy Score, and renders at least one graph visualization on the frontend.

quotes:
1. Crop Yield Prediction Module
- Inputs:
    - Soil Type
    - Rainfall (mm)
    - Temperature (°C)
    - Humidity (%)
    - Fertilizer Usage
- Use Random Forest Regression model
- Train on sample agriculture dataset
- Output:
    - Predicted Yield (tons per hectare)
    - Accuracy Score
    - Graph Visualization

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend form validates numeric ranges (no negative rainfall/humidity, etc.) and shows inline errors.
Calling the backend returns a numeric predicted yield and a numeric accuracy score.
Frontend renders a chart (e.g., bar/line) showing the prediction in context (e.g., feature contributions, or comparison to sample baseline values).
A sample agriculture dataset is included in the repo as a static file and referenced in code (for demo/visualization).

requirements.text: Plant Disease Detection module: provide a leaf image upload UI, send the image to the backend, and return Disease Name, Confidence Percentage, and Suggested Treatment.

quotes:
2. Plant Disease Detection Module
- Upload leaf image
- Use CNN model
- Train on PlantVillage dataset
- Output:
    - Disease Name
    - Confidence Percentage
    - Suggested Treatment

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend supports uploading common image formats (at least PNG/JPG) and shows a preview before submission.
Backend accepts the uploaded image payload (or its encoded representation) with size/type validation and returns a structured result containing diseaseName, confidence, and treatment.
Frontend displays the result in a clear card layout and records the result into the user’s history.
If input is invalid (missing image/too large/unsupported type), user sees a clear error message.

requirements.text: Smart Irrigation Recommendation module: implement an end-to-end flow that accepts inputs (Soil Moisture Level, Weather Condition, Temperature) and returns Water Required (liters/acre) and Irrigation Recommendation (Yes/No).

quotes:
3. Smart Irrigation Recommendation
- Inputs:
    - Soil Moisture Level
    - Weather Condition
    - Temperature
- Output:
    - Water Required (Liters per acre)
    - Irrigation Recommendation (Yes/No)

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend validates inputs and shows error states for missing/invalid values.
Backend returns a numeric waterRequiredLitersPerAcre and a boolean/enum recommendation.
Result is shown on the page and stored in per-user history.

requirements.text: Add a visualizations page that compares module outputs and “model accuracy comparison” charts using a frontend charting library.
acceptanceCriteria: Visualizations page shows at least: (1) crop yield accuracy score trend or distribution, (2) disease detection confidence distribution, (3) irrigation recommendation breakdown (Yes/No) over history.
Charts render from real stored history returned by the backend (not hardcoded).

requirements.text: Implement authentication using Internet Identity and gate history/persistence features behind the authenticated principal (no custom username/password storage).
acceptanceCriteria: Users can sign in/out with Internet Identity.
When signed out, module pages still render but any “Save to history / View history” features prompt sign-in (or history is hidden).
Backend associates stored results with caller principal.

requirements.text: Add robust error handling end-to-end: client-side validation, backend input validation, and consistent error messaging in the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: All backend endpoints return typed error responses for invalid payloads and unexpected failures.
Frontend displays errors in a consistent component (toast/alert) and prevents duplicate submissions while loading.

requirements.text: Provide production-ready project documentation: README with local run steps for the Internet Computer template, clear module descriptions, and how to test each API from the frontend; add code comments where necessary to explain data flow and assumptions.

quotes:
Deliverables:
- Instructions to run locally

Features:
- README file
- Comments in code
- Requirements.txt file

acceptanceCriteria: README includes: prerequisites, install steps, how to run locally, how to deploy locally with dfx, and how to use each module UI.
Documentation explains platform constraints vs the originally requested Python/ML stack and what is implemented instead.
Key logic sections (backend prediction/recommendation logic and frontend API calls) include brief explanatory comments.

requirements.text: Include sample datasets/artifacts in-repo as static assets suitable for demo/visualization (e.g., a small CSV/JSON for agriculture yield examples and a small label/treatment mapping for diseases).

quotes:
Modules Required:
- Train on sample agriculture dataset

acceptanceCriteria: Repo includes at least one small sample dataset file for crop yield visualization and one disease label→treatment mapping file.
Frontend loads these assets without requiring any external network calls.

requirements.text: Create a “History” section (either per module or centralized) that lists the authenticated user’s saved runs with timestamps and the key output fields, and allows clearing history.
acceptanceCriteria: Authenticated users can view a list of past results for each module including timestamp and output summary.
Users can clear their history; backend deletes the stored entries for that principal.
UI updates immediately after clearing (refetch or optimistic update).

constraints: Backend must be implemented in Motoko as a single-actor canister (no Flask/FastAPI).
No external databases (no MySQL/SQLite); persist data using canister stable storage.

No external ML frameworks (no scikit-learn / TensorFlow/Keras) can run in-canister; any “model” behavior must be implemented with lightweight deterministic logic and/or precomputed parameters stored in-repo.
Frontend must use the existing template’s immutable hook/component paths without editing them (compose them instead).
Do not add third-party authentication beyond Internet Identity.
nonGoals: Training a real Random Forest Regression model or CNN model inside the deployed app.
Downloading or bundling the full PlantVillage dataset in the deployed app (only small demo assets/mappings).
Implementing username/password signup/login with password storage or reset flows.
Integrating external Python services or external REST microservices.

required: Wide dashboard hero illustration with fields, sensors, and crops in a clean flat style (dashboard-hero.dim_1600x600.png)
